As Meat Loves Salt by Maria McCann. It is devastatingly sad. I didn't even want to go on for a day or so after reading it and I couldn't even imagine starting a new book. What a novel.

Looking for Mr. Goodbar by Judith Rossner.

The Road by Cormac McCarthy. Seriously. This book is one of the saddest I've ever read.

The Road was beyond sad! It was a level of tragic that I found hard to get through objectively.

With most apocalyptic books, I've been able to remain distant and safe. The Road was not like that at all. It drew me in, grabbed my heart and did not let go.

The Road is incredibly dark, both literally and metaphorically.

You get to watch as a young boy's earnest hope for a world possibly rejuvenated and redeemed by the acts of man get crushed by the inertia of page after page of silent weeping for mankind's fall. In this world, EVERYTHING is gray. The trees, the people, the minds, the moralities, the actions, the ground, the little wreckage -- everything.

That book is an enchanting eulogy for a horribly fragmented world devoid of solace.
